focus: Design the least-invasive validator-policy and archive-inclusion contract, preserving new v4 findings as errors while allowing only evidence-backed deterministic treatment of legacy residuals.
answeredQuestions: Least-invasive policy is strict-by-default with explicit per-rule historical evidence exceptions.
Safe archive behavior is explicit, separately enumerated, and read-only by default.
keyQuestions: Which residual rule classes can deterministic transformations clear without authored content, and what does each cost?
Which residuals are v4-only contract additions versus defects already present under v3?
Which residuals require the least validator-policy change, and how can new v4 findings remain errors?
Why are archived packets skipped, and what explicit include behavior is safe?
What ordering and idempotence proof make the upgrade command deterministic and failure-reporting?
noveltyJustification: Converts the provenance split into an explicit four-lane migration policy and exposes archive inclusion as a separate scope and audit contract rather than an incidental tool default.
ruledOut: global generated-metadata grandfather as final proof
reusing active repair defaults for z_archive
treating z_future as equivalent to z_archive
